body: The spec's central operational risk is data availability, and it is handled in a way that converts failure into a pass. Materials Project and AFLOWlib are DFT databases of crystalline phases; neither, to my knowledge, exposes a `material_type` field flagging amorphous/metallic-glass entries, nor measured thermal-expansion coefficients for glasses with thermal-history metadata (FR-009). The spec nonetheless assumes both exist and sets a target of ≥500 entries, but then writes: 'if <500 are available, the system proceeds and logs a warning, treating this as a valid pass condition.' A pipeline that ingests, say, 40 entries and proceeds to 5-fold cross-validation stratified by alloy family would satisfy the acceptance test while producing results too thin to support any claim about a composition-CTE mapping. The honest mechanical fix is a hard lower bound below which the pipeline halts with a distinct 'insufficient data' status, so that a null result is not confused with a data-availability failure. Two lesser points: (a) filtering by 'presence of the keyword "glass" in the entry description' (FR-001) will admit crystalline entries whose descriptions mention glass-forming ability or processing; (b) the permutation test with ≥1000 iterations cannot resolve p-values below ~1/1001, so 'p < 0.05' claims from the idea document are fine but finer significance language should be avoided. The branch label '001-gene-regulation' appears to be a copy-paste remnant from an unrelated project and should be corrected before implementation work begins.
